---
title: "PROC UNIVARIATE"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# Show an HTML document of sas_html() in an isolated frame, so its style
# sheet does not mix with the page.
show_html <- function(doc, height = 320) {
  esc <- gsub('"', "&quot;", gsub("&", "&amp;", doc, fixed = TRUE), fixed = TRUE)
  knitr::asis_output(sprintf(
    '<iframe srcdoc="%s" style="width: 100%%; height: %dpx; border: 1px solid #c1c1c1;"></iframe>',
    esc, height))
}
```

```{r setup}
library(sasonr)
```

PROC UNIVARIATE describes the distribution of numeric variables: moments,
basic measures of location and variability, tests for location, quantiles and
extreme observations.

```{r}
res <- sas_run("
options nocenter;
data vitals;
  input sbp @@;
  datalines;
128 124 135 131 118 121 140 126 133 119
;
run;
proc univariate data=vitals;
  var sbp;
run;
")
cat(res$listing, sep = "\n")
```

## The HTML output

The same tables as an HTML document, from `sas_html()`:

```{r, echo = FALSE}
show_html(sas_html(res), height = 700)
```
